results.name: Finset.sum_product'
results.source_text:
@[to_additive /-- The sum over a product set equals the sum of the fiberwise sums. For rewriting
in the reverse direction, use `Finset.sum_product` -/]
theorem prod_product' (s : Finset γ) (t : Finset α) (f : γ → α → β) :
    ∏ x ∈ s ×ˢ t, f x.1 x.2 = ∏ x ∈ s, ∏ y ∈ t, f x y :=
results.docstring:
The sum over a product set equals the sum of the fiberwise sums. For rewriting
in the reverse direction, use `Finset.sum_product`

results.name: Finset.sum_finset_product'
results.source_text:
@[to_additive]
theorem prod_finset_product' (r : Finset (γ × α)) (s : Finset γ) (t : γ → Finset α)
    (h : ∀ p : γ × α, p ∈ r ↔ p.1 ∈ s ∧ p.2 ∈ t p.1) {f : γ → α → β} :
    ∏ p ∈ r, f p.1 p.2 = ∏ c ∈ s, ∏ a ∈ t c, f c a :=

results.name: Finset.sum_union
results.source_text:
@[to_additive]
theorem prod_union [DecidableEq ι] (h : Disjoint s₁ s₂) :
    ∏ x ∈ s₁ ∪ s₂, f x = (∏ x ∈ s₁, f x) * ∏ x ∈ s₂, f x := by

results.name: Fin.prod_univ_succ
results.source_text:
/-- A product of a function `f : Fin (n + 1) → M` over all `Fin (n + 1)`
is the product of `f 0` times the remaining product -/
@[to_additive /-- A sum of a function `f : Fin (n + 1) → M` over all `Fin (n + 1)` is the sum of
`f 0` plus the remaining sum -/]
theorem prod_univ_succ (f : Fin (n + 1) → M) :
    ∏ i, f i = f 0 * ∏ i : Fin n, f i.succ :=
  prod_univ_succAbove f 0
results.docstring:
A product of a function `f : Fin (n + 1) → M` over all `Fin (n + 1)`
is the product of `f 0` times the remaining product

results.name: Finset.coe_prod

@[to_additive (attr := simp, norm_cast)]
theorem coe_prod (s : Finset ι) (f : ι → Finset α) :
    ↑(∏ i ∈ s, f i) = ∏ i ∈ s, (f i : Set α) :=
  map_prod (coeMonoidHom : Finset α →* Set α) _ _

instance (d : Dimension) (M : Type) [AddCommSemigroup M] :
    AddCommSemigroup (WithDim d M) where
  add_comm m1 m2 := by
    ext
    simp [add_comm]

results.name: Physlib.PiTensorProduct.instAddCommMonoidElim_physlib
results.source_text:
/-- Given two maps `s1` and `s2` whose targets carry an instance of an additive commutative
  monoid, the target of the sum of these two maps also carry an instance thereof. -/
instance : (i : ι1 ⊕ ι2) → AddCommMonoid ((fun i => Sum.elim s1 s2 i) i) := fun i =>
  match i with
  | Sum.inl i => inst1 i
  | Sum.inr i => inst2 i
results.docstring:
Given two maps `s1` and `s2` whose targets carry an instance of an additive commutative
monoid, the target of the sum of these two maps also carry an instance thereof.
